clue.text: Return in support of sudden attack

parts.note: pro means in favour of, supporting
a fit is a sudden attack of illness or temper

explanation.surface: A counter-strike made in support of a sudden attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A financial return on money laid out is a gain, the excess earned over cost.

clue.text: Piece of boxing ring

definitions.meaning: one of the timed sessions that make up a boxing bout
a circle, something circular in shape

explanation.surface: Part of the ring where a boxing match takes place.
explanation.definitionFit: A bout of boxing is split into three-minute sessions, and a ring is a circular shape.

clue.text: Fighter, very new plane, finally included in Air Force unit

indicators.note: the final letters are placed within the RAF unit, as something included sits inside it

parts.note: a flight is a small unit of aircraft in an air force

indicators.note: takes the closing letter of each of the three words before it

explanation.surface: A brand-new fighter plane is added to an Air Force squadron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fighter' looks like the plane, but it is a boxer; 'finally' takes the last letters of very, new, plane, and 'included in' puts them inside the Air Force unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer in one of the lightest weight classes is a kind of fighter.

clue.text: Having worked hard as diplomat, finally reduced friction

indicators.note: picks out only the closing letter of the word diplomat

parts.note: oiled means lubricated, so friction was reduced

explanation.surface: A diplomat who laboured to ease tensions between parties.
explanation.definitionFit: To toil is to labour strenuously, so the past tense means laboured hard.

clue.text: Beer pub brought back is for author

indicators.note: both the drink and the pub are read from the end backwards

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
a bar is a pub
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone collecting beer from a pub on behalf of a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' turns ALEBAR into RABELA, then IS follows.
explanation.definitionFit: François Rabelais was the French Renaissance writer of Gargantua and Pantagruel.

clue.text: Doctor's work providing meaningful options, in other words

definitions.text: Doctor's work providing meaningful options, in other words

parts.words: Doctor's work providing meaningful options, in other words
parts.note: Peter Mark Roget was a physician whose famous book lists words of similar meaning to choose from

explanation.surface: A physician's report offering several sensible treatments, to put it differently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' suggests a medical text, but Roget was a doctor who compiled a book of synonyms; 'in other words' is both the phrase and what the book supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: Roget's compilation is the classic reference of synonyms, offering alternative words with the same meaning.

clue.text: Religious type converted this unfortunate sailor first

indicators.note: the sailor's name is placed at the start, ahead of the rearranged word

parts.note: Billy Budd is the doomed sailor of Herman Melville's novella, hanged at the end

indicators.note: the letters of this are changed into a new form, as a convert is changed

explanation.surface: A believer who brought round an ill-fated seaman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' suggests religious conversion, fitting the surface, but it is the anagram signal; 'first' puts Melville's sailor ahead of the rearranged word.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of the Buddha's teaching is an adherent of a world religion.

clue.text: Incomplete fortune I had collected? It's all there

indicators.note: the synonym for fortune loses its last letter, so it is not complete

parts.note: luck means fortune
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone wondering whether the money they gathered is the full sum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collected' looks like gathered money but means composed, as does 'all there'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucid means clear-headed and sane, mentally composed and fully in possession of one's wits.

clue.text: Unit's invading one Asian country or another

indicators.note: one piece enters the middle of the other, as an army invades a land

parts.note: India is a country in Asia
unit's read as 'unit is', ones: a one is a unit

explanation.surface: A military force invading an Asian nation, or perhaps a different one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unit' looks military, but it is a numeral one; 'or another' makes the answer a second Asian country.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a further nation in Asia, a different one from India.

clue.text: Improvised reason for mistrial?

definitions.meaning: put together hastily from what was to hand
a panel of jurors fixed or tampered with would cause a trial to collapse

explanation.surface: Wondering what makes a court case collapse.
explanation.definitionFit: Makeshift rigging on a ship gave the term for anything rigged up temporarily, and a rigged jury voids a trial.

clue.text: A medic has turned in final piece of work

indicators.note: the pair is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: doc is short for doctor, a medic

explanation.surface: A doctor submitting the last part of an assignment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses A DOC as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A coda is the closing passage of a musical piece or other work.

clue.text: Supporter of something in newspaper he tore to pieces

parts.note: an ad, an advertisement, appears in a paper
taken as written
rent is the past tense of rend, to tear apart

explanation.surface: Someone backing a cause while a man shreds the paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tore to pieces' looks like an anagram signal, but it is RENT, the old past tense of rend; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An adherent is a follower or backer of a party, cause or faith.

clue.text: Covering up corporal punishment

explanation.surface: Concealing physical punishment of schoolchildren.
explanation.definitionFit: Hiding means concealing, and a hiding is also a sound thrashing.

clue.text: Amphibian, in confusion, crossing river

indicators.note: the confusion word stretches across the river letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a fog is a state of mental confusion

explanation.surface: A muddled amphibian making its way over a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A frog is a tailless amphibian that lives near water.

clue.text: Metal is used in rake, to adopt standard procedure

indicators.note: the metal and is are placed inside the rake

parts.note: a roué is a rake, a debauched man
tin is a metal
taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions for a garden rake made of metal, following set practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rake' looks like a garden tool, but it is a dissolute man, ROUE; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To routinise is to make something a routine, settling it into a fixed habitual procedure.

clue.text: Most delicious wine in trial

indicators.note: the wine goes inside the word for trial

parts.note: a test is a trial
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: A wine tasting judged the finest wine on trial.
explanation.definitionFit: Tastiest is the superlative of tasty, full of flavour.

clue.text: Bizarre instances happening all the time

indicators.note: something bizarre is strange and out of order, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Strange events that keep occurring nonstop.
explanation.definitionFit: Incessant means continuing without pause, unceasing.

clue.text: Deeply understood fellow Democrat embracing party

indicators.note: the two letters wrap around the party word, holding it

parts.note: an at-home is a party held in one's own house

explanation.surface: A Democrat who grasped a colleague's meaning while hugging the party line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' looks political after 'Democrat', but it is AT HOME, a social gathering at someone's house.
explanation.definitionFit: To fathom is to measure depth, and figuratively to grasp fully.

clue.text: A bit of baggage from legal actions

parts.note: a suit is a lawsuit, a legal action
a case is a legal action in court

explanation.surface: Luggage obtained from lawsuits.
explanation.definitionFit: A case for carrying clothes when travelling is one item of luggage.

clue.text: Rabbit caught by bowler, perhaps

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
a bowler is a kind of hat, so 'perhaps' marks an example

explanation.surface: A rabbit dismissed by a bowler in a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowler' suggests cricket, but it is a bowler hat, the hard round British felt hat.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang, rabbit and pork means talk, so to rabbit is to talk on.

clue.text: Negligent, so fail again in one's aim?

definitions.text: so fail again in one's aim?
definitions.meaning: read as ..., to miss the target a second time

explanation.surface: Careless enough to miss the target once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Remiss means lax or careless in performing a duty.

clue.text: Some tack —- it's cheesy

indicators.note: only part of the following words supplies the letters

explanation.surface: A remark that a bit of tacky stuff is cheesy.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'tack' through 'it's' into 'cheesy'; the whole clue also defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitsch is tacky, sentimental art or decor in poor taste, so it is tack, and cheesy.

clue.text: Broadcaster swore atrociously — what could be worse?

indicators.note: the letters of swore are made a mess of, done atrociously

explanation.surface: A radio presenter cursed on air, and nothing could be worse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcaster' looks like a presenter, but it is someone scattering seed; 'what could be worse?' hints that WORSE also rearranges to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sower broadcasts seed, scattering it over a field by hand.

clue.text: A poet's work, including one volume that's repellent

indicators.note: the poem word contains the two letters within it

parts.note: verse is poetry, what a poet writes
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A collection of poetry with one book that disgusts readers.
explanation.definitionFit: Aversive means causing aversion, so unpleasant and repellent.

clue.text: Announcement when showing artwork in Eastern state

indicators.note: the painting goes inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for Virginia, a state on the US east coast
an oil is an oil painting

explanation.surface: An oil painting exhibited in Virginia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eastern' suggests the Orient, but it is Virginia on the US Atlantic coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Voilà, French for 'there it is', is exclaimed when revealing something.

clue.text: Panorama that's very wide at the sides

indicators.note: the two letters stand on either side of the abbreviation

parts.note: W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide
i.e., id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A broad landscape that stretches far on both sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the sides' places V and W around IE.
explanation.definitionFit: A panorama is a wide view over a landscape.

clue.text: Notes alarming changes to one area

indicators.note: the letters of alarming are altered in order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Memos warning of worrying alterations to a single zone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alarming' looks like an adjective describing the changes, but it is the fodder; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Marginalia are notes scribbled in the margins of a book.

clue.text: Man travels round British Isles

indicators.note: the man and travels words go around the British letter

parts.note: he is a male pronoun
rides means travels

explanation.surface: A man touring the British Isles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like the Isle of Man, but it is HE; 'British Isles' looks like one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hebrides are island chains off the west coast of Scotland.

clue.text: Region as turned over to local ruler

indicators.note: region word and as are read together backwards

parts.note: a part is a region, as in parts of the country
taken as written

explanation.surface: A territory handed over to a regional governor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned over' reverses PARTAS as a whole; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A satrap was a provincial governor in ancient Persia, now any subordinate local ruler.
